identity.name: Kingdom of Osroene
native_names: Orhay (Urhay), the Aramaic name of Edessa

capitals.name: Edessa (Şanlıurfa)

region.text: Osroene around Edessa, the Euphrates loop to the north and west (without Nisibis)

ledger.note: 132 BC: the Abgarid kingdom of Osroene appears at Edessa. Infobox 'Established 132 BC'; the text says Osroene acquired independence 'from 136 BC'. The page names Edessa and says the area was 'perhaps roughly coterminous' with the Roman province, not a boundary. [fix me-06-b: region now without Nisibis, see the _-63 keyframe.]

region.text: Osroene around Edessa, which 'had acknowledged his authority' by 95 BC

ledger.note: By 95 BC: Osroene a Parthian vassal. 'by 95 BC, the northern Mesopotamian kingdoms of Adiabene, Gordyene, and Osrhoene had acknowledged his authority' (Mithridates II page; the conquest is 'the following year', so the exact year is not given). Mirrors parthian-empire /ledger/28 (vassal_start kingdom-of-osroene, -95, confidence 3). The Osroene page has only 'Osroene was generally allied with the Parthian Empire' (undated) and nothing on Mithridates II.

region.text: the western district of Osroene, which became a Roman dependency

ledger.note: 66/65 BC: Osroene leaves the Parthian sphere. Phraates III controlled Mesopotamia 'except for the western district of Osroene, which became a Roman dependency' (Roman-Parthian Wars page, in the Pompey-era passage, no separate year). Mirrors parthian-empire /ledger/37 (vassal_end kingdom-of-osroene, -66, confidence 2). The Armenian tributary status under Tigranes (Osroene infobox map caption, no year) is not drawn: it would overlap the Parthian span above, and the Tigranes page has no sentence on Osroene.

region.text: Osroene, 'absorbed into the Roman Empire in 114 as a semiautonomous vassal state'

ledger.note: 114: Osroene a Roman vassal. 'absorbed into the Roman Empire in 114 as a semiautonomous vassal state' (Osroene page); Trajan's page: Abgar VII 'submitted to Trajan publicly, as a Roman protectorate' (115). The year is the Osroene page's; the same page also puts the end of independence in 116.

region.text: Osroene, taken with the rest of northern Mesopotamia

ledger.note: 115: the vassalage becomes annexation. 'In 115, the Roman emperor overran northern Mesopotamia and annexed it to Rome as well' (Trajan page); the Osroene page ends the kingdom's independence in 116 under Quietus. See the 115 loss.

region.text: Osroene, taken with the rest of northern Mesopotamia (without Nisibis)

ledger.note: 115: Trajan takes northern Mesopotamia and Abgar VII submits. 'In 115, the Roman emperor overran northern Mesopotamia and annexed it to Rome as well'; Abgar VII 'submitted to Trajan publicly, as a Roman protectorate'. The Osroene page says 'absorbed into the Roman Empire in 114 as a semiautonomous vassal state' and elsewhere that Lucius Quietus put 'an end to Osrhoene's independence in 116'. The Trajan page's own chronology is 'uncertain'.

region.text: Osroene as a Roman client under Yalur and Parthamaspates (without Nisibis)

ledger.note: 118: a Roman-backed king rules Osroene again. After 'Trajan died in 117 before he could renew the war', Hadrian 'willingly returned to the status quo ante, surrendering the territories of Armenia, Mesopotamia, and Adiabene back to their previous rulers and client-kings' (Roman-Parthian Wars page, no year given; quote corrected by reviewer me-06-b); the Osroene page's list has Yalur and Parthamaspates in 118-122 after an interregnum of 116-118.

region.text: Osroene as a Roman client under Yalur and Parthamaspates

ledger.note: 118: a Roman-backed king rules Osroene again, a client of Hadrian's Empire. The Osroene page's king list has Yalur and Parthamaspates in 118-122 and says that in 123 'Osroene was established as a client kingdom of the Empire' (Ma'nu VII); the 118 status is a reading of 'Roman-backed', the 123 sentence confirms it (confidence 2 for 118; it would be 3 from 123).

123: the Abgarid dynasty is restored under Ma'nu VII. 'Osroene was established as a client kingdom of the Empire' after the dynasty was restored with Ma'nu VII (123-139); Parthamaspates, Hadrian's king since 118, goes.

region.text: Osroene, held by the Parthian nominee while Rome moved up the Euphrates (without Nisibis)

ledger.note: 163: the Parthians intervene in Osroene. 'In 163, while Statius Priscus was occupied in Armenia, the Parthians intervened in Osroene', deposing Mannus (Ma'nu VIII) for a nominee who 'would remain in office until 165'; 'before the end of the year ... Roman forces had moved north to occupy Dausara and Nicephorium'.

region.text: Osroene, held by the Parthian nominee

ledger.note: 163: the Roman client is displaced. 'In 163, while Statius Priscus was occupied in Armenia, the Parthians intervened in Osroene' and deposed Mannus (Ma'nu VIII).

region.text: Osroene under Wa'el, 'Installed by the Parthians'

ledger.note: 163-165: Osroene a Parthian nominee kingdom. King list: 'Wa'el, son of Sahru | 163-165 AD | Installed by the Parthians' (Osroene page); the 161-166 page: the nominee 'would remain in office until 165'. Drawn beside the contest with roman-empire (same dates); the contest zone is the blend, this is the Parthian tint.

165: Rome retakes Edessa and reinstalls Mannus. 'In 165, Roman forces, perhaps led by Martius Verus and the V Macedonica, moved on Mesopotamia': Edessa was reoccupied and Mannus reinstalled; the Parthians retreated to Nisibis and lost it too. The war ended in 166.
165: the Parthian nominee falls. 'In 165, Roman forces ... moved on Mesopotamia': Edessa reoccupied, Mannus reinstalled.

region.text: Osroene under Mannus, 'King Mannos, friend of the Romans'

ledger.note: 165: Mannus (Ma'nu VIII) is reinstalled and Osroene is a Roman client again (the 161-166 page; the Mesopotamia page: Northern Mesopotamia, including Osroene, 'were left under local vassal rulers').

region.text: the remaining territory of the kingdom

ledger.note: 214: the client kingdom ends with Caracalla's annexation ('the remaining territory incorporated into the Roman province of Osroene'); see the loss and dissolve events.

region.text: the remaining territory of the kingdom, now the Roman province of Osroene (without Nisibis)

ledger.note: 214: Caracalla deposes Abgar IX and annexes Osroene. 'the remaining territory incorporated into the Roman province of Osroene'; the page's lead says 214, the text 213 and the king list 212-214.

214: the Kingdom of Osroene ends. Abgar IX Severus (212-214) is 'deposed by the Romans'; Ma'nu IX (214-240) and Abgar X (240-242) are 'maybe in name only', and a rump 'briefly existed during the reign of Roman emperor Gordianus III (238-244)', a debated point left undrawn.

wars.name: Crassus' invasion of Parthia
wars.outcome: Parthian victory at Carrhae (53 BC); Osroene's king Abgar II, 'an ally of the Roman general Marcus Licinius Crassus', died later that year. No Osroene border moved.
wars.note: The Battle of Carrhae lay on Osroene's soil (Carrhae/Harran) but the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign
wars.outcome: Osroene submitted in 115 as a Roman protectorate and lost its independence by 116; Hadrian's withdrawal left the Euphrates the frontier again.
wars.note: Dates for the fall of Osroene differ between the pages (114, 115, 116).

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 161-166
wars.outcome: Roman victory with 'minor Roman gains in upper Mesopotamia'; Edessa reoccupied and Mannus reinstalled in 165; Nisibis stayed Roman. Osroene remained a client kingdom.
wars.note: Parthian intervention in Osroene 163-165; Roman advance across the Euphrates late 163 and on Edessa and Nisibis in 165.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian war of Septimius Severus
wars.outcome: Severus 'mounted an invasion of the kingdom and possibly annexed some of its territory' but 'allowed the Abgar VIII to retain his kingdom'; Rome kept northern Mesopotamia round Nisibis and Singara.
wars.note: The Mesopotamia page says he organised Osroene as a full province (no year); the Osroene page's reading is followed. No zone is drawn because no land is named.

wars.name: Roman annexation of Osroene
wars.outcome: Caracalla deposed Abgar IX and the remaining territory became the Roman province of Osroene (214).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any page; the Euphrates loop on the north and west is a natural frontier and the eastern limit (Nisibis?) is uncertain.

Disagrees with the Osroene page ('possibly annexed some of its territory').

notes:
Pages opened: Osroene, Trajan's Parthian campaign, Roman-Parthian War of 161-166, Mesopotamia (Roman province), Roman-Parthian Wars (five: the budget).

Area: no infobox area; the page only says 'perhaps roughly coterminous' with the Roman province. Cliopatria's 50 k km2 is 2.7 times the gazetteer's Osroene region (18.5 k km2, Sanliurfa only); the shape's bounding box runs 37.96-41.54E, 35.7-37.9N (Nisibis side in the east, the Euphrates bend in the south), which the page's Euphrates-loop and Nisibis remarks loosely support; unverified.

Disagreements: independence 132 BC (infobox) vs 136 BC (text); absorption by Rome 114 (Osroene page), 115 (Trajan page), 116 (Quietus, Osroene page); the end 213 vs 214 (Osroene page); Severus 195 leaves Abgar VIII his kingdom (Osroene page) or makes Osroene a full province (Mesopotamia page, no year).

Left undrawn: Armenian overlordship under Tigranes (a map caption, no date); the rump kingdom of 238-244; the Parthian-held interlude of 163-165 is drawn as a contest with roman-empire; 195 'possibly annexed some of its territory' (no land named). Cliopatria has no shape for 114-126 and 161-164; new keyframes osroene_118 and osroene_161 carry the 127 shape back.

For the roman-empire dossier (eu-04): it has a 214 gain from kingdom-of-osroene (matches the loss here) but no events for the 115 annexation, the 118 return and the 163-165 contest on Osroene. For the parthian-empire dossier (me-06-a): it records Osroene as a vassal from about 95 BC (Mithridates II page) and as leaving the Parthian sphere in 66/65 BC; the Parthian Empire page itself says nothing on those years. Anthemusia (Batnae), a semi-autonomous principality annexed by Rome in 115, is a possible minor dossier.

[fix me-06-b, 2026-10-19] Reviewer verdict fail, repaired. (1) Vassal chain added (shape without Nisibis as region): Parthian from 95 BC (Mithridates II page) to 66 BC (Roman-Parthian Wars page; mirrors parthian-empire /ledger/28 and /37); Roman 114 to 115 (Osroene page: 'semiautonomous vassal state'; ends with the 115 annexation); Roman from 118 (client of Hadrian; the 123 sentence confirms) with a Parthian-nominee interruption 163-165 (king list 'Installed by the Parthians') and a Roman restart in 165, to 214. The contest of 163-165 with roman-empire stays beside the Parthian vassal. The Armenian tributary status under Tigranes is not drawn (the infobox map caption has no year, the Tigranes page has no sentence on Osroene, and it would overlap the Parthian span). (2) All ten Cliopatria shapes (-63..207) and the new keyframes -132, 118 and 161 now exclude the 40 km circle round Nisibis (verdict adjust, confidence 2), and the ledger regions follow. Disagreement: the Osroene page says the eastern boundary 'may have extended to Nisibis'; I followed the reviewer because the Adiabene page dates the grant of Nisibis to Izates to 36, the 161-166 page has Rome take it in 165 and the Mesopotamia page has it the provincial capital in 198. After the cut the largest shape is about 48 k km2, still 2.6 times the gazetteer's Osroene region; no page gives an area (Osroene, Mesopotamia re-opened), so the area question stays open and the shapes are not claimed to be verified. (3) The misquote of the Roman-Parthian Wars page is also corrected in the 118 keyframe note. (4) Thin items: Septimius Severus page (opened) says Severus annexed 'the Kingdom of Osroene' as a new province (194 on its sequence) and that Abgar IX was 'titular King of Osroene but essentially only the ruler of Edessa' (197): a third reading beside the Osroene page ('possibly annexed some of its territory', 195) and the Mesopotamia page ('organized Osroene as a full province'); no land is named, so no shape is cut and the kingdom is drawn whole to 214. Gordian III page (opened): nothing on Osroene, so the 238-244 rump stays undrawn. For eu-04: roman-empire has no events for the 114-115, 118 and 163-165 stretches; its /ledger/87 gain of Osroene in 214 matches. For eu-04 and me-06-b's Adiabene: both hold Nisibis from 36 and 165; see the Adiabene note.
